chunks: Abi (rah) from Sa’d ibn Abdillah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Sa’d ibn Abi Khalaf from Abi al-Hasan Musa (a.s.) who said:

The obligatory prayers, when offered in their prime time fulfilling all their conditions, have a sweeter scent than a branch of the aspen tree when it is taken from its tree in its fragrance, scent, and freshness. So it is obligatory upon you to offer them at the prime time.

key_terms.قَضِیبِ الْآسِ: A branch of the aspen tree

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for praying obligatory prayers at their earliest time?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights the superior spiritual merit of offering obligatory prayers at their earliest time (awwal al-waqt), using the metaphor of the fresh, sweet scent of an aspen branch to illustrate the purity and freshness of such devotion. This emphasis on promptness reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of valuing not just the validity of prayer, but the excellence (fada'il) of performing it with immediate attentiveness upon the entry of its time.
